question: Suppose $\vec{a}$ and $\vec{b}$ are nonzero vectors and $\theta$ is the angle between them. Which of the following represents the area of a triangle with sides $\vec{a}$ and $\vec{b}$ and can also be interpreted geometrically as the magnitude of the  projection of one vector onto the perpendicular of the other?
explanation:
Area of triangle with sides $\vec{a}, \vec{b}$ is $\frac{1}{2}|\vec{a}\times\vec{b}|$.

This value is also interpreted as half the area of the parallelogram formed by $\vec{a}, \vec{b}$, whose area is $|\vec{a}\times\vec{b}|$.

Projection of one vector onto the perpendicular of the other (i.e., the height relative to base given by other vector) multiplied by the base gives the parallelogram area, so half of that is triangle area.

Correct answer: B) $\frac{1}{2}|\vec{a}\times\vec{b}|$
